svg.title: DDIA 10 · CONSISTENCY & CONSENSUS: sketchnote
svg.text: How machines agree despite everything in Chapter 9: linearizability, ordering without trusted clocks, and consensus.
Alice: "it's over!" Bob refreshes after hearing her
Linearizable: once ANY reader sees the new value, all later reads must too
Linearizability means every operation appears to take effect
atomically at one point in time, consistent with real-time order.
If the resizer reads a lagging storage replica, it resizes the
old image. Two channels give a race.
time first: roughly sorted, no coordination, only as ordered as the clocks
Auto-increment is a SPOF; UUIDv4 is unordered.
Snowflake/UUIDv7: time first, roughly sorted, as ordered as
Order: compare counter, tie-break by node ID → a TOTAL order consistent with causality
The limit: the order is only known after the fact.
HLC stays near wall-clock time and never goes back; vector
clocks detect concurrency. Strict real-time order needs a
Raft · Paxos · Zab implement it; ZooKeeper and etcd sell it as a service
Single value, shared log, CAS/fetch-and-add, atomic commit:
solve one fault-tolerantly and you solve them all.
entry committed once a MAJORITY (3/5) has it
If the leader goes silent, a follower times out, increments the
term, and asks for votes. A majority makes it leader. A higher
Membership via ephemeral nodes that vanish when a session
dies; config and shard maps that clients watch for changes.
Answer per feature: booking and payment are CP, search and
feeds are AP. Mention PACELC latency cost.
Not 2PC (blocking, coupling). Use a saga + outbox + idempotent
Leader election via ZooKeeper or etcd (consensus), lease +
Needs linearizable compare-and-set: one strongly consistent store
(Spanner, CockroachDB, or a single-leader region for usernames).
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.
